questions.question: Which device provides the electrical energy to make a torch work?
questions.explanation: The electric cell (or battery) acts as the primary source of electrical energy.

questions.question: What do we call the complete path through which electric current flows?
questions.explanation: An electric circuit provides the necessary continuous loop for current flow.

questions.question: What is the main function of a switch in a circuit?

options.text: To open or close the circuit

questions.explanation: A switch is a control mechanism to complete (close) or break (open) the electrical path.

questions.question: Which specific part of the electric bulb glows to give light?
questions.explanation: The thin tungsten filament heats up due to resistance and emits light.

questions.question: In a circuit diagram, what does the longer straight line of a battery symbol represent?
questions.explanation: Standard schematic symbols use a longer line for the positive terminal and a shorter, thicker line for the negative.

questions.question: Materials that easily allow electric current to pass through them are called:
questions.explanation: Conductors, generally metals, permit the easy flow of electrons.

questions.question: Which of the following objects is an insulator?
questions.explanation: Rubber heavily resists electrical flow, making it an excellent insulator.

questions.question: When a switch is placed in the 'OFF' position, the circuit is said to be:
questions.explanation: Turning the switch OFF creates an air gap, rendering the circuit open.

questions.question: How many terminals does a standard single electric cell have?
questions.explanation: It possesses a positive terminal (metal cap) and a negative terminal (metal disc).

questions.question: What exactly is a battery?

options.text: A combination of two or more cells

questions.explanation: Multiple cells connected properly in series constitute a battery.

questions.question: Why are household electrical wires usually covered with plastic or rubber?
questions.explanation: Insulators cover the live conductors to ensure human safety during handling.

questions.question: In standard circuit diagrams, which direction is conventional electric current shown to flow?
questions.explanation: Convention dictates current flows from the positive to the negative terminal.

questions.question: If a bulb's filament is broken, it is said to be:
questions.explanation: A broken filament creates a permanent gap, meaning the lamp is fused.

questions.question: Which of the following connection setups will form a properly working battery?
questions.explanation: Cells must be placed in series (positive to negative) to correctly compound their voltage.

questions.question: If a wooden stick is placed in a circuit instead of a connecting wire, will the bulb glow?
questions.explanation: Wood is a poor conductor (insulator) and will arrest the flow of current.

questions.question: How does an LED differ from a standard incandescent bulb when connected in a circuit?

options.text: LED only conducts current in one specific direction (polarity)

questions.explanation: LEDs are diodes and require correct polarity (positive to positive, negative to negative) to function.

questions.question: What is the original source of energy stored inside an electric cell?
questions.explanation: Internal chemical reactions are converted into electrical energy.

questions.question: You connect a circuit, but the bulb doesn't glow. Which is NOT a logical reason for this failure?
questions.explanation: A closed switch completes the circuit; if the bulb fails, the reason lies elsewhere.

questions.question: Which metal is most commonly utilized for manufacturing electrical wires?
questions.explanation: Copper offers an excellent balance of high conductivity, flexibility, and cost.

questions.question: Why can the human body receive dangerous electric shocks?

options.text: Because the body is an insulator
Because the human body conducts electricity
Because the body generates its own electricity

questions.explanation: The human body contains water and dissolved salts, making it a viable conductor.

questions.question: Two bulbs are connected one after another in a single line (series). What happens if the filament of the first bulb breaks?

options.text: The second bulb stops glowing entirely
The second bulb glows the same

questions.explanation: In a series circuit, any break halts the current for the entire path, shutting down all components.

questions.question: Which statement regarding an electrical switch is scientifically false?

options.text: It completes or breaks a circuit
It controls the flow of current
It is the source of electric current
When OFF, there is an air gap

questions.explanation: A switch regulates current but generates none; the cell is the source.

questions.question: Why is the filament of an incandescent bulb hermetically encased in glass?

options.text: To protect the superheated filament from reacting with oxygen and burning out

questions.explanation: If exposed to air, the extreme heat would cause the tungsten filament to instantly combust.

questions.question: A student connects the longer lead of an LED to the negative terminal and the shorter lead to the positive terminal. What occurs?
questions.explanation: Reversed polarity blocks the current in an LED, preventing it from glowing.

questions.question: What is the most reliable experimental method to test if a material is a conductor or an insulator?

options.text: Connect it between two free ends of an open circuit with a working bulb

questions.explanation: Using the material to bridge a gap will verify its conductivity based on whether the bulb lights up.

questions.question: What happens if a rubber band is connected between the ends of an electric circuit?

options.text: Current stops because rubber acts as an insulator

questions.explanation: The rubber introduces a gap of high resistance, halting the electron flow.

questions.question: Why do electricians specifically use screwdrivers with plastic or rubber handles?

options.text: The material acts as an insulator, preventing current from entering the body

questions.explanation: The handle breaks the conductive path between the live wire and the electrician's hand.

questions.question: Which of the following sources provides Direct Current (DC)?
questions.explanation: Cells and batteries produce DC, where electrons flow steadily in a single direction.

questions.question: You have six cells (A through F) and want to find which one is dead. How do you accurately test them?

options.text: Connect each one individually to a working bulb in a simple circuit

questions.explanation: Isolating each cell in a known working circuit provides empirical proof of its voltage capacity.

questions.question: What physically creates the high resistance 'air gap' in an open circuit?

options.text: Moving the switch to the 'OFF' position, separating the metal contacts

questions.explanation: The mechanical action of the switch separates the conductive paths, filling the space with insulating air.
